title: Tickets Overview
summary: Explains how a ticket differs from a meter's flowing data and how a new ticket is created for a single point in time.

sections.heading: What Is a Ticket
sections.body: A ticket is similar to a meter in that it belongs to a meter, but where a meter has flowing data captured continuously (for example, each hour), a ticket represents data for a single point in time rather than a periodic record.
key_points: A meter captures flowing data continuously, e.g. each hour.
A ticket represents a single point-in-time record rather than a periodic one.

sections.heading: Creating a New Ticket
sections.body: To create a ticket, click on the meter to see its empty data grid, then choose the option to create a new ticket. Because a ticket is a one-time record rather than a periodic one, the product and applicable temperature (and similar fields) must be selected manually for that entry.
key_points: New tickets are created from the meter's empty grid via a 'create new ticket' option.
Ticket entries require manually selecting fields such as product and temperature, since there is no periodic record to draw from.

faqs.question: How does a FLOWCAL ticket differ from a meter's flowing data?
options: A ticket represents a single point-in-time record rather than continuous data
A ticket only exists for gas meters
A ticket replaces the need for a location
A ticket is generated automatically every hour like periodic data
faqs.explanation: The What Is a Ticket section explains a meter captures continuous flowing data while a ticket is a single point-in-time record.

faqs.question: Why must fields like product and temperature be selected manually when creating a new ticket?
options: Because tickets are periodic and copy prior values automatically
Because there is no periodic record for the ticket to draw values from
Because tickets do not support products
Because manual import always overrides ticket fields
faqs.explanation: The Creating a New Ticket section notes these fields are manual since a ticket, unlike a periodic record, has no prior data to draw from.
